lessons.claim: When a sketch writes local driving ('move one particle') and a bulk observable (G'(ω), G''(ω)) on the same page, those two are not the same quantity -- it has to be raised as an ambiguity at intake. Single-point driving gives a local response K*(ω) [N/m], and the GSER conversion G*=K*/(6πa) has already been measured to be invalid in this family (what the bead feels is not a medium but its neighbouring beads). The only reading that gives all four of the sketch's goals (G', G'', the response time, stress propagation) from one measurement is **two-point microrheology** (shake one particle and watch the correlated displacements of distant particles) -- G* is legitimate in the long-wavelength limit and the phase lag with distance is the stress propagation itself.

not_verified: the only grounds that the two-point reading is the user's intent is the consistency that 'all 4 goals come out of one measurement'. Reporting the single-point K*(ω) is a legitimate choice too, and since the driving is the same both can be extracted from the same run, so they may not need to be separated.
